tasks.title: Performance hardening — target 100 on every page, desktop + mobile
tasks.notes: All Phase 1 deps are done. Structural levers already shipped — measure before optimizing. 34 of 35 routes ship only 3,209-byte `app.js` with no React on non-island pages.

prep.what: Run Lighthouse on representative pages, read the scores, then fix the top performance blockers (image sizing, font loading, CLS) to drive toward 100.
prep.understand: The site already ships a tiny JS bundle (3KB app.js) on most pages — that's done. What remains is: (1) images without explicit width/height cause layout shift (CLS), (2) fonts may be render-blocking without `font-display: swap`, (3) images might not be WebP/AVIF or lazy-loaded. The rule is measure first, optimize second — do NOT guess what's slow.
approach: Run Lighthouse on the home page and one service page (Chrome DevTools → Lighthouse tab, or `npm run lighthouse` if configured). Note baseline scores.
For each category under 100, expand the Lighthouse recommendations. Focus on Performance first: largest contentful paint (LCP), total blocking time (TBT), CLS.
Fix the 2-3 highest-impact items: add explicit `width`/`height` to all `` tags, add `loading='lazy'` to below-fold images, and confirm fonts use `font-display: swap` in CSS.
Re-run Lighthouse after fixes to confirm score improvement, then repeat for the remaining routes.
resources: Laravel Blade templates in `resources/views/` for image tags

prep.what: Build the `/contact` page with a contact form that posts to a local API route — no real email delivery yet, just logs the payload.

Create `app/api/contact/route.ts` — a POST handler that parses the JSON body, `console.log`s it, and returns `NextResponse.json({ok: true})`.

Create `app/contact/page.tsx` — a client component with controlled inputs for name, email, message (and any other fields from the content file). On submit, POST to `/api/contact` and show a success state.

tasks.title: Search
tasks.notes: Client-side filter over mock products is fine for now. Real search swaps in when Shopify is wired.

prep.what: Add a `/search` page with a text input that filters the mock product list client-side — real Shopify search will swap in later.
prep.understand: The mock product data is defined somewhere in the project (likely a `lib/` or `data/` file that exports an array of product objects with name, handle, description, etc.). Client-side filtering means: keep a search query in React state, filter the mock array by `product.title.toLowerCase().includes(query.toLowerCase())`, render matching product cards.
approach: Find where mock products are defined — search for `MOCK_PRODUCTS` or look in `lib/` / `data/` for the product array. Note the shape (id, title, handle, price, image, etc.).
Create `app/search/page.tsx` as a client component with a `useState` for the search query and a text input.
Filter the mock products array by the query string (title + description match) and render results using the existing product card component.
Add a search icon/link in the nav if not present; confirm the page renders empty state gracefully when no results match.

Existing product card component (used on collection pages)
